newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus plans to open more free economic zones.
newsitem.headline: Belarus plans to open more free economic zones.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Belarus plans to open a free economic zone in its capital city and one in each of its six regions by the end of March, First Deputy Prime Minister Pyotr Prokopvych said late on Monday.
"The president will establish a free economic zone around Minsk's international airport, at Gomel, and one in every region by the end of the first quarter of 1997," he told a news conference.
He said a German company making ecological products had already signed a 14 million mark deal in the Brest zone.
"We expect the volume of investments to increase to $60 million in this zone by the end of this year," he said.
Prokopvych said the zones were part of a government plan to increase foreign investment in the country of 10 million people.
Economy Ministry figures put total foreign investment at $123.9 million in 1996, down from $157.3 million in 1995.
